No actionable defect in the frozen fish-favorites candidate. Scoped source, the shared policy core, and the optimized3 evidence agree. Confirmation4 is rejected.

The frozen files match optimized3 `source-final.json` and receipt `compiler-fixtures-1793374519204764792` (tree `52fbe671459e76370cc9cf73b05dd94a008fce3f220c25478611e58b61c49380`, 1504 inputs). Checked on disk: schema `ff9d6205…`, `js_unicode.rs` `32515868…`, tests `1342626c…`, benchmark `e000ea69…`, archived schema `30b6361c…` and test `4fb11013…`.

## Findings

None.

## Checks that closed

Alias policy matches the archived TypeScript helpers. `normalize_favorite_alias` trims, then `lowercase_ascii_bounded` (40, ASCII-only), then `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$/` and the four `FISH_VOICES` keys. `make_favorite_alias_iter` does NFKD, strips UTF-16 units U+0300–U+036F, lowercases, collapses non-alphanumeric runs, trims edge separators, slices 40 bytes, falls back to `voice`, and suffixes from 2. Final sigma stays non-ASCII, so the ASCII projection does not need the contextual scan. Unpaired UTF-16 fails the alias check the same way a surrogate fails the JavaScript regex.

The collision set is bounded. At `channel_fish_voice_favorites.schema.rs` lines 196–198 the capacity is `size_hint().0 + FISH_VOICES.len()` on the pre-filter iterator. The public API and the add path both iterate a slice (or a map of one), so that lower bound is the real length. `filter_map(JsString::as_str)` only drops names that cannot equal an ASCII alias, which leaves spare capacity. The suffix loop reuses one `String` truncated to `base_len`.

`add_with` / `rename_with` / `remove_with` emit the same filters, `$push` / `$pull` / arrayFilters, 0..=20 attempts, settings migration before the favorite compare-and-swap, and the three rename fallthroughs as the TypeScript source. `MongoFavorites` is a concrete adapter: `__v: 0` on upsert `$setOnInsert`, and `updatedAt` only on the non-upsert settings update. The concrete test expects no `createdAt` on that update. Malformed BSON rejection and unknown-field projection match the typed-record contract. Lone-surrogate ids are replaced at the BSON boundary; the in-memory return keeps the original units, and a second add or rename against the stored U+FFFD id conflicts or is not found. That matches the driver probe and the test at lines 830–840.

Benchmark medians from the stored samples match the report. Same input SHA `c4c38e94…` and provenance SHA `5984251f…`. Sorted sample index 3 is Node/Rust ns: valid 158.645890625 / 80.617578125, invalid 7652.4270625 / 89.04303125, make ASCII 866.68428125 / 458.5545, Unicode 883.24996875 / 835.660875, collisions 2081.6051875 / 2150.15259375. Checksums match across runtimes. Collisions are slower in Rust on this helper median. Invalid-case times are not comparable: JavaScript builds an `Error` with a stack, and Rust returns a `Result`.

## Unverified limits

This review did not run Cargo, Node, Mongo, Clippy, or containers, and did not rehash all 1504 inputs. The receipt records that tree hash and `success: true`.

`compiler-fixtures-1793374519204764792.log` shows the fish binary 6/6 passed in 0.29s with zero ignored, including `concrete_mongo_favorites_and_legacy_default` and `source_oracle_pure_and_protocol`, then the release ASCII-lower, NFKD, and NFC oracles (0.27s, 0.34s, 0.46s). The three later `Checking` steps do not echo argv, so Clippy `-D warnings`, minimal, and all-features are not identifiable from that log. Nothing in the log shows those steps failing.

The 21-miss `favorites_conflict` path and the rename fallthroughs are proven on `ReplayRepo` (`force_miss` / `miss_change`), not as a real Mongo schedule. The concrete run covers one capacity race, one same-id add, one distinct-id alias split, and one rename collision. That is one passing schedule each.

`js_compat.rs` is a direct trim dependency and is absent from the functional oracle file list (it is in the benchmark provenance). Trim’s exclusion of U+0085 matches ECMAScript WhiteSpace and LineTerminator by inspection. The oracle normalization corpus has no NEL case, and this fixture log does not show the `js_compat` unit test.

Confirmation4 stays rejected: `interrupted-run.json` is `interrupted-without-driver-receipt`, `benchmark_confirmation_accepted: false`, container `full-rust-5ad445d87cdc`. No confirmation4 number is used.
